answer: The strongest lever is simple: score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because bridge only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. In practice hollow is enforced by the ledger itself: Jurors see the identity's full answer chain, so a template match is detectable in one pass. Any sparrow approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
